title: Distributed Key-Value Store
summary: Build a horizontally-partitioned key-value store with replicas and a coordinator that tracks who owns each key.
narrative:
One database node can't hold the dataset anymore, and it certainly can't serve the read volume. You need a key-value store that scales out: split the keyspace into shards spread across many nodes, and keep more than one copy of each shard so a dead node isn't lost data.

The hard part isn't storing bytes — it's agreement. When a request arrives, something has to know which node owns that key, and every part of the system has to agree on that mapping even as nodes join, leave, and fail. That's the job of a coordination service like ZooKeeper or etcd: it holds the authoritative shard map and cluster membership, so a stateless coordinator tier can route each read and write to the node that actually owns the key. Layer a cache in front to soak up the hottest keys, and reads fly.

Assemble it: clients hit the load balancer, which spreads requests over a fleet of stateless coordinator nodes; those nodes consult ZooKeeper/etcd for placement and then read or write the right NoSQL replica, caching hot keys on the way back. Keep clients away from storage — routing is the coordinator's job.

functional: Store and retrieve values by key across many nodes
Partition the keyspace into shards spread over the cluster
Route each request to the node that owns the key
Keep at least two copies of every shard
nonFunctional: Losing a single storage node must not lose data
Hot keys are served without hitting storage every time
The cluster agrees on shard ownership as nodes come and go
constraints: Clients reach data only through the coordinator tier
Shard placement is resolved via the coordination service
capacity: Tens of terabytes spread over many shards
specs.tradeoff: Sharding with a coordinator buys near-unlimited horizontal scale, but at the cost of a coordination dependency and the complexity of routing and rebalancing keys.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring to watch replica lag and shard balance across the cluster.

missions.label: Add a NoSQL Database to hold the partitions
Route Client traffic through the Load Balancer
Balance requests across the coordinator tier
Resolve shard placement via the coordinator
Serve hot keys from a Cache
Add Monitoring for replica lag and shard balance

topologyRules.message: Clients must never reach storage directly — routing belongs to the coordinator tier.
Every key lookup must be routed through the coordinator tier before it touches a NoSQL node.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two NoSQL nodes so every shard has a replica and one node failure isn't data loss.
The coordinator tier must be wired to ZooKeeper/etcd to resolve which node owns each key.

hints: Clients hit the Load Balancer, which spreads requests across stateless coordinator nodes (Web Servers). Keep clients well away from storage — the coordinators own the routing.
The coordinators can't guess which node holds a key. Wire the Web Server to ZooKeeper/etcd so it reads the authoritative shard map before touching storage.
Add a second NoSQL node so every shard has a replica and losing one isn't data loss, then front the store with a Cache for hot keys. Monitoring closes the loop on replica lag.
